title: Flatness and tensor reduction for the finite constant completion tower
statement: theorem finiteSystem_flat_and_reduction (J : GrothendieckTopology C) (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A] (I : Ideal A) [∀ (n : ℕ) (U : Cᵒᵖ), Module (A ⧸ I ^ (n + 1)) (adicTerm J A (finiteSystemUnder J A I) n U)] (htower : ∀ (n : ℕ) (U : Cᵒᵖ), IsScalarTower A (A ⧸ I ^ (n + 1)) (adicTerm J A (finiteSystemUnder J A I) n U)) : (∀ (n : ℕ) (U : Cᵒᵖ), Module.Flat (A ⧸ I ^ (n + 1)) (adicTerm J A (finiteSystemUnder J A I) n U)) ∧ (∀ (m n : ℕ) (U : Cᵒᵖ), ∃ e : TensorProduct A (adicTerm J A (finiteSystemUnder J A I) m U) (A ⧸ I ^ (n + 1)) ≃ₗ[A] adicTerm J A (finiteSystemUnder J A I) (min m n) U, ∀ (b : adicTerm J A (finiteSystemUnder J A I) m U) (a : A), e (b ⊗ₜ[A] Ideal.Quotient.mk _ a) = a • adicTransition J A (finiteSystemUnder J A I) m (min m n) (Nat.min_le_left m n) U b)

source.place: Tags 093M and 0912, sectionwise flatness and tensor reduction

proof.text: For R = A/I^(n+1), the given scalar tower forces mk(a) acting on a section to equal a acting on that section. Naturality of the sheafification unit identifies the latter action with multiplication by the constant R-section mk(a). Since every element of R has a representative a, the identity additive equivalence from the given section module to the canonical R-section module is R-linear.

Use the already proved ringSectionsFlat helper in ConstantCompletionFlatAndQuotientsFlatness: its ringModuleLinearEquiv identifies the constant ring sections with the sections of the constant regular R-module. Apply the flat-section clause of constantModule_section_properties over the Noetherian ring R, then transport flatness along the identity linear equivalence of the previous step. Only this finite-level helper is used, not the completed-flatness theorem.

Let B be the sections of the constant A-ring sheaf, eta:A->B its sheafification unit, and f_k:B->S_k the actual finite quotient section map. The existing constant quotient theorem says that f_k is surjective with kernel (I^(k+1)).map eta. The quotient cone identity gives q composed with f_m = f_min for the actual transition q:S_m->S_min. In particular q is surjective. Mapping its kernel back and forth across the surjection f_m gives ker(q) = (ker(f_min)).map f_m.

The structural map A->S_m is f_m composed with eta. If n<=m, the previous kernel identity is directly ker(q)=(I^(n+1)).map(A->S_m). If m<=n, the image of I^(m+1) is zero because it is the image of ker(f_m), and I^(n+1)<=I^(m+1), so the same identity holds with both sides zero. Compose Mathlib Algebra.TensorProduct.quotIdealMapEquivTensorQuot (inverted and restricted to A), Ideal.quotientEquivAlgOfEq for this kernel equality, and Ideal.quotientKerAlgEquivOfSurjective. On b tensor mk(a) the composite is q(a smul b)=a smul q(b), by A-linearity of the actual transition.
